body.directive: When attributing a convicted hallucination to a responsible step, name only a step that can host the error: its own event text, tool arguments, or prose must contain the specific erroneous content (a fabricated value, an anomalous tool output, or an unsupported claim) that is carried into the delivered result. Before naming a step, check its recorded text for that erroneous content; if the candidate step's text does not contain it, move the attribution to the earliest step in the transcript whose text does contain it, such as the search or note step that first asserts a false figure, or the final-answer step that submits an unverified anomalous tool output.
body.not_when: Do not move the attribution when the currently named step's own text already contains the erroneous content that reaches the delivered result, and do not apply this constraint when the judge did not convict a hallucination or the packet has no delivered result to anchor the error.

claim.expected_behavior: The step tracer names a responsible step whose own recorded text contains the erroneous content that reaches the delivered result, so the named step can host the error instead of being an unhostable step.
